question: What does a Dietary Diversity Score actually measure?

options.A: The total financial cost of a family weekly food supply
options.B: The physical weight of food a person eats every single day
options.C: The exact number of daily calories eaten by a patient
options.D: The total number of food groups consumed over a period

explanation: Spot on! It counts how many different food groups are in a person's meals during a set time, usually the past 24 hours. Great way to check if someone is getting a balanced mix! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: Why can eating only one type of staple food (like just garri or corn pap) be dangerous for a person's health?

options.A: It raises the blood pressure to dangerous levels within hours
options.B: It leads to hidden hunger and a lack of essential micronutrients
options.C: It automatically causes rapid and uncontrollable weight gain
options.D: It stops the digestive system from absorbing any water at all

explanation: You got it! Relying on just one food means missing out on all the vital vitamins and minerals found in other food groups. Variety is key! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: Which of these is counted as a healthy food group in standard dietary scoring?
explanation: That's right! Ugwu, spinach, and other dark greens are packed with essential nutrients like iron and folate to keep the body strong. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: Why are items like sugary soft drinks left out of standard food groups?

options.A: They are too expensive for rural families to buy
options.B: They contain too much water and zero calories
options.C: They spoil too quickly in warm tropical climates
options.D: They offer little to no real nutritional value

explanation: Exactly! Dietary scores focus on nutrient-packed foods that actually build health, rather than empty calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: How does vitamin C help your body when you eat it along with beans?

options.A: It increases the absorption of plant-based iron
options.B: It prevents the protein in beans from causing gas
options.C: It turns the complex carbohydrates into simple sugars
options.D: It slows down digestion so you feel full longer

explanation: Brilliant! Vitamin C acts like a helpful helper, making it much easier for your gut to absorb the iron found in plant foods like beans. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: What is a major perk of getting your vitamins from real food instead of pills?

options.A: Pills are always completely fake and contain no actual vitamins
options.B: Whole foods provide fiber and a complex nutritional matrix
options.C: Whole foods cost nothing at all to produce or purchase
options.D: Pills take up to a week to dissolve in the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! Whole foods come with extra bonuses like fiber and natural plant compounds that supplements just can't copy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge to eating a diverse diet in Nigeria?

options.A: Seasonal changes that affect fresh crop yields
options.B: Cultural taboos restricting certain foods for mothers
options.C: High market prices and general household poverty
options.D: Excessive availability of free vitamin supplements

explanation: Correct! Free supplements are a good thing, not a barrier. Poverty, seasonal shifts, and strict food customs are the real hurdles families face. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: How do traditional food taboos negatively affect community health?

options.A: They cause farmers to grow only cash crops instead of edible vegetables
options.B: They prevent vulnerable groups like pregnant women from eating nutrient-dense foods
options.C: They force families to spend all their income on expensive imported foods
options.D: They make the soil too acidic for crops like beans and maize to grow

explanation: You nailed it. Cultural rules often keep protein-rich foods away from the pregnant women and children who need them the most. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: What is a common health problem in children who eat a poor, low-diversity diet?

options.A: Complete immunity to common childhood tropical diseases
options.B: Rapid increase in bone density and excessive height
options.C: Sudden development of high blood pressure in infancy
options.D: Increased vulnerability to infections and stunted physical growth

explanation: That's right. Missing out on diverse nutrients weakens their immune system and slows down their growth, leading to frequent illnesses. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with signs of malnutrition, mentioning the child only eats corn pap daily. What is this a classic sign of?

options.B: Monotonous diet leading to hidden hunger and malnutrition
options.C: A healthy traditional weaning practice for infants
options.D: An allergic reaction to processed maize products

explanation: Spot on! Relying on just one carb source without adding proteins or veggies will quickly lead to serious nutrient shortages. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: A nursing mother says she cannot afford expensive baby formula or imported supplements. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain that homemade food has no nutritional value for babies
options.B: Show her how to enrich local family staples with mashed beans and green leaves
options.C: Advise her to wait until the child is five years old to eat solid food
options.D: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately and buy cow milk instead

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Always encourage affordable, locally available foods that families can easily prepare and sustain. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: Why are immunization and antenatal clinics such great places to teach mothers about nutrition?

options.A: Doctors perform surgical procedures to improve digestion during these visits
options.B: Patients have extra money to spend on luxury foods when visiting the clinic
options.C: Hospitals provide free meals to every single visitor who walks through the door
options.D: They bring mothers and vulnerable young children into regular contact with nurses

explanation: You got it! Routine clinic visits give us the perfect chance to reach and educate the exact people who need nutritional guidance the most. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)
